title: Sessions show visibly when the agent is waiting on a script, job or queue rather than thinking

requirements.text: While a foreground tool call (e.g. a long Bash) has been running past a threshold (~10s), the session reports a distinct state naming what it is waiting on (the command's description) and since when
requirements.check: eye: in an app session have the agent run a 60s sleep-style command; the tab and grid pane show the waiting-on state with its label and elapsed time, then return to working when it ends

requirements.text: When the agent ends its turn with a background task still running (run_in_background, Monitor) or blocked on a claim/queue, the session shows the waiting-on state instead of done, until that task finishes
requirements.check: eye: agent starts a background command and ends its turn; the session shows waiting-on, not done; when the command exits it changes

requirements.text: An agent can declare a wait explicitly: genlock wait "WHAT" [--until ...] sets the state and clears on its next tool call or a genlock wait --clear
requirements.check: manual: genlock wait "build queue" in an app session shows that label; the next tool call clears it

requirements.text: The waiting-on state looks different at a glance from working, waiting-for-you and done (its own colour/icon, e.g. an hourglass), in tabs, grid panes and the dashboard, and never triggers the needs-you sound or notification
requirements.check: eye: all four states side by side are distinguishable without reading text; waiting-on makes no sound

requirements.text: Hook and state tests cover the new state; app builds and core tests pass
requirements.check: node tests/run.mjs && cd app && swift build && swift test

text: Add a waiting-on-non-agentic-work state, shown visually
user_said: when agents are doing background work, and waiting on some background script to finish, or waiting on a queue to release, i cannot tell if its doing work. i need it to be able to have a feature that indicates its waiting on something non-agentic..... visually

text: Queued. State today comes from hooks in lib/voice.mjs cmdSessionState (~L55): UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse=working, Notification=waiting (on the user), Stop=done; written to the session channel state.json, read by app (AppModel/SessionsView/Snapshot.swift). Add PreToolUse to start a timer on long calls; background tasks need tracking past Stop. Name it to avoid clashing with existing 'waiting' (= needs you). lib/voice.mjs not held by others; tests/run.mjs held by T-W6QH3.

A queued wait and a running job show differently: 'queued behind bikes-5' vs 'running bag-probe 2m10s', fed by nightmaremode's game/tools/testq.sh calling genlock wait (sessions inherit GENLOCK_APP_CHANNEL, so a script can report)

answers.observed: Probe in live nightmaremode queue: queued -> running -> cleared; tests 10/10 new node checks, WaitTests 5/5; screenshot showed hourglass in tabs
answers.cause: Hypothesis tested: Claude Code transcript carries <task-id>..</task-id> with <status> for background completion; checked in this session's own transcript
answers.absence: Long-foreground-command display and holding-after-Stop not watched on screen; sessions opened before the update lack the PreToolUse hook until restarted
answers.assumption: Mine: 10s threshold; background tasks pruned only when a hook fires, so a holding badge can linger until the agent wakes on the notification
answers.falsify: A session holding after its background job finished and the agent processed the notification
